family: The single total certificate-prefix language specified in proof.md and family.py. For actual length N, choose k as the least prime at least the least positive B with B^5>32*N^3; read k input bits as the lower coefficients of a monic degree-k polynomial Q over F_2, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, and evaluate the descending-power BK symmetric polynomial on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding, r=ceil((N-k)/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)). Output 0 for N=0 or the explicit failed guards in proof.md. The output is the constant coefficient in F_2[Z]/Q. All k prefix bits are included in N; Q is input, not advice.
theorem: For the single total uniform polynomial-time certificate-prefix family defined in proof.md and family.py, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-4k-8d_N+8 for all sufficiently large integer N, where W=r(r+3)/2, H=(t-1)(t+2)/2, A0=(t-1)k-H-(r-t+1), d_N=1+W+max(A0,floor(r(k-1)/(t+1))), k=O(N^(3/5)), and d_N=O(N^(4/5)). At every accepted tuple, d_weight-d_N>=min(r-t+1,floor(kr/t)-floor(r(k-1)/(t+1)))>=2, where d_weight=1+W+max(floor(kr/t),(t-1)k-H); thus the finite guarantee for this SAME family strengthens the individual-weight predecessor by at least 16 gates. Consequently liminf over all integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N>=4 in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length N. Moreover (4k+8d_N-8)/(4k+8d_old-8) tends to 1/2 over all integer lengths, where d_old=floor(kr/t)+kt+r(r+1)+1; this compares proved same-family remainder certificates, not actual circuit complexities.
